parsed.answer: For Mara's Larch project, the only approved delivery mode established in the evidence is BATCH-0-741, chosen on 2026-08-01. The 2026-08-08 test of REPLAY-0-632 did not approve a delivery-mode change. The 2026-08-22 record says to keep the "August 15 delivery choice," but the supplied evidence does not identify what that Larch choice was, so it does not establish a different approved delivery mode. As of 2026-08-22, the retry policy is RETRY-0-907, superseding RETRY-0-108. In the signed Kestrel-0 return policy, the two exception identifiers are CUSTOM-0-7c2 for custom-made goods and DEFECT-0-9b4 for quality defects; DRAFT-0-2d1 is only an unauthorized draft.

citations.quote: 2026-08-01. Mara started project Larch. They chose BATCH-0-741 for batch delivery. The initial retry policy was RETRY-0-108.

2026-08-08. Mara reported that BATCH-0-741 lost updates during GATE-0-519 outages. The team tested REPLAY-0-632, which restored the missing updates. No change of delivery mode was approved at this meeting.

2026-08-22. Mara reviewed Larch. Keep the August 15 delivery choice. For the next outage, use the recovery procedure validated on August 8. The retry policy is now RETRY-0-907, superseding RETRY-0-108. No budget owner has been appointed.

Kestrel-0 signed return policy. Ordinary goods have a 7-day return window. The complete exception list consists of two clauses: custom-made goods use exception CUSTOM-0-7c2; quality defects use exception DEFECT-0-9b4 and are exempt from the 7-day limit. Both exception identifiers must be retained when listing all exceptions. The old informal draft listed only DRAFT-0-2d1 and has no authority.
